messages:
mike: heads-up: saw a host decode p99 bump around 06:12 UTC after yesterday's kernel-selector change. p99 +52ms on preparse path. dashboard snippet: https://perf.corp/4329999999 :alarm_clock:

infra-bot: alert: host-preparse.p99 delta=+52ms window=7m affected=host-runtime-12[ab]

anya: can you share the top stacks? trying to figure out whether this is CPU-copy or grpc overhead.

mike: attached a collapsed stack sample. most time in Tokenizer::align_copy and then a spike in grpc::writev. looks like extra memcpy then small writes.

```
# collapsed
Tokenizer::align_copy  36.4ms
ProtoUnpack::parse      18.0ms
grpc::writev            16.7ms
EventLoop::poll         3.1ms
```

leo: selector rolled `simd-align-v2` into canary yesterday. that kernel does 16-byte align memmoves for vector loads. good for long seqs, but if host is doing many tiny token emits it's extra work.

anya: batching estimator uses kernel_cost table to pick batch targets. did we refresh the cost table after landing simd-align-v2?

mike: nope, config still has old costs. estimator now underestimates simd-align-v2 cost and reduces batch target which increases the number of batches. net effect: more host-side overhead + more tiny writev calls.

leo: we should gate the selector until we re-run microbench and update the cost table. short mitigation: add a runtime clamp to treat simd-align-v2 cost = max(simd-align-v2_cost, scalar_cost). i can push a CL.

ops: there's a feature-flag runtime.kernel.gate_simd_align_v2 that we can flip without restart. want me to set it on canary?

anya: yes please flip on canary and emit a metric per-request "kernel_chosen" for 12h so we can correlate. also add a small kv-prefetch probe to see if hits drop when batch size shrinks.

ops: flag flipped on canary at 06:35 UTC (runtime.kernel.gate_simd_align_v2=true)

mike: monitoring canary -> p99 decreased ~40ms so far. writev count per request dropped 58%. kv hit delta ~0.8% (small).

leo: i'll run full rebench suite for simd-align-v2 vs scalar across seq lengths [8,16,32,48,64] and batch sizes [8,16,32]. will post numbers. looking specifically at memcpy bytes and syscall counts.

anya: also: implement a micro coalescer in ingress proxy to group writev within 150us or until 1KB aggregate. that should reduce syscall tail impact if small frames are unavoidable. can we add as opt-in?

mike: good plan. maybe coalescer default off and enable per-backend that shows high small write counts.

ops: noted. will create canary for coalescer with feature flag ingress.coalesce_writev_ms=0.15 and emit metrics grpc.writev_coalesced_ratio.

infra-bot: created ticket PERF-2026-045: kernel-cost-mismatch -> batching fallback amplification. escalation: update rollout checklist to include cost-table refresh and small-write smoke test.

mike: owners: @leo rebench & cost table patch, @anya instrument kernel telemetry + kv probe, @ops flip coalescer on canary. i'll keep watching infra and will revert if noise increases. thanks all :raised_hands:

ops: canary deployed for coalescer at 07:02 UTC.

mike: follow-up: please capture perf flamegraph after rebench so we can compare memcpy hotspots. will collect postmortem after we have rebench numbers.
